title: Investigating chemical reaction
competency: Conduct an experiment to show a simple chemical reaction (burning magnesium).

keywords.def: A process that changes substances into one or more new substances.

en.text: Rub a magnesium ribbon, hold it with tongs and burn it. It gives a very bright light. A white powder forms: magnesium oxide. The powder does not bend, is not shiny and will not burn again. A new substance formed, so a chemical reaction occurred: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

screens.title: Predict first
screens.ask: Shiny magnesium ribbon burns in a flame. What do you expect to be left?
screens.after:
A white powder, magnesium oxide, is left.
The magnesium joined with oxygen from the air. It did not vanish.
The powder is a new substance.

screens.title: Experiment 3.1: Burning of magnesium ribbon
paras: Objective: to investigate the chemical reaction.
Apparatus: burner, crucible, a pair of tongs.

screens.title: Procedure
steps: Take about 5 cm of magnesium ribbon. Rub it gently. Notice its colour and hardness.
Hold it with a pair of tongs and burn it.
Collect the substance formed in a crucible.
Examine it. Feel it. Notice its colour.

screens.caption: Hold the ribbon with tongs, never with your hand.

screens.title: Hazards!
paras: Burning magnesium is extremely bright and gives some ultraviolet light.
Do not look directly at it.
It is very hot. Do not touch it. Keep it away from things that burn.

screens.title: Apparatus and safety
screens.ask: Tap each one before you start.
items: Gives the flame that lights the ribbon.
Hold the burning ribbon. Never use your hand.
Burning magnesium is extremely bright. It gives some ultraviolet light.
Do not touch it. Keep it away from things that burn.

screens.title: Before and after burning
items: A shiny metal. It bends. It burns with a very bright light.
Magnesium oxide. Not shiny. It does not bend. It will not burn again.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A process that changes substances into one or more new substances.

screens.text: Observation 1: what are the reactants when magnesium burns?
screens.why:
Burning needs oxygen from the air.
The magnesium joins with this oxygen.
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
So the reactants are magnesium and oxygen.
Magnesium oxide is the product, not a reactant.
screens.clue: What in the air helps burning?

screens.text: True or false: the white powder is shiny and bends like the ribbon.
screens.why:
The ribbon is shiny and bends.
The powder is white, not shiny, and does not bend.
New properties show a new substance.
So the statement is false.
screens.clue: Compare the powder with the ribbon.

screens.text: Observation 3: did a chemical reaction occur when the ribbon burned?
opts: Yes: a new substance with new properties formed
screens.ans: Yes: a new substance with new properties formed
screens.why:
The product is a white powder, not a shiny ribbon.
It has new properties: it does not bend or burn.
So a new substance formed.
Yes, a chemical reaction occurred.
Heat alone does not prove a reaction; the new substance does.
screens.clue: Is the product the same as the ribbon?

screens.text: Lab safety: why must you not look straight at burning magnesium?
opts: It is extremely bright and gives ultraviolet light
screens.ans: It is extremely bright and gives ultraviolet light
screens.why:
The Hazards box warns about the light.
Burning magnesium is extremely bright.
It also gives some ultraviolet light.
So do not look straight at it.

test.text: Experiment 3.1: what is left after magnesium burns?
test.why:
The ribbon joins with oxygen.
The product is magnesium oxide.
It is a white powder.

test.text: Lab safety: what do we hold the burning ribbon with?
test.why:
Burning magnesium is very hot.
Fingers or paper would burn.
So we hold the ribbon with tongs.

test.text: Name the product of burning magnesium.
test.why:
Magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide.
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
No chlorine is present, so not magnesium chloride.
The product is magnesium oxide.

test.text: True or false: magnesium oxide burns again if heated.
test.why:
The book observes that the white powder will not burn again.
The magnesium has already joined with oxygen.
So the statement is false.

test.text: Evidence: which observation proves a NEW substance formed?
opts: The product is white and not shiny, unlike the ribbon
test.ans: The product is white and not shiny, unlike the ribbon
test.why:
A new substance has new properties.
The ribbon is shiny. The product is white and not shiny.
Getting hot alone does not prove a new substance.
The length of the ribbon tells nothing about a change.
So the white, not shiny product is the proof.
